analysis: Both supplied units are BASE-side excerpts of CHANGELOG.md (lines 2387-3014), which are historical release notes outside the changed ranges (base changed range is only 11-13; head adds lines 11-808). They contain no executable code, configuration or permissions, so nothing in them can regress a threat-model control. I reviewed the text for claims that might invalidate threat assumptions. The entries describe prefix-cache behaviour (SSD checkpoints, HMAC-keyed names, authenticated complete checkpoints, tenant/model/prompt/runtime identity gates, cache kill switch) and App Attest shadow rollout. These are consistent with T-041, T-053, T-054 and TB-011 and are retained history, not new behaviour. The actual PR change is in the head-side patch, which was only partially visible: a v0.10.6 candidate section describing two-Mac clusters with RDMA over Thunderbolt, `darkbloom cluster`, the `cluster_runtime` registration field, release-derived cluster approvals and pair-serving grants, and a local-API-only mode using the `darkbloom start --local` key. That patch excerpt is truncated, and the source for it is not in this batch. This is new attack surface beyond the current threat model, which has no TB for the Thunderbolt/RDMA inter-Mac link, cluster peer authentication, or how prompt plaintext and KV state are shared between peers. Because the code is not supplied, I cannot confirm a concrete regression and do not assert one. A later pass should check (1) whether the threat model needs a cluster trust boundary covering peer authentication, plaintext exposure to the second Mac, and the effect on T-041 cache scope and the A-016 per-connection authorization, (2) whether self-reported `cluster_runtime` facts could drive approvals without Apple-attested evidence, and (3) whether the unauthenticated local API key mode is bound to localhost. These are open questions for the integration pass and the changelog text alone proves nothing.
